newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX natgas scores more gains with cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX natgas scores more gains with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to rally late Tuesday in active trade, still driven by a tight physical market and a wave of technical buying after prices broke resistance early, market sources said.
At 1410 EDT, June, which expires tomorrow, was up seven cents at $2.355 per million British thermal units. July was 5.6 cents higher at $2.35. Most others also were up.

"Basis (next month) seems pretty tight. I don't think we'll see much downside near-term," said one East Coast trader, noting steady injection demand and light incremental loads this month have been enough to tighten the balance.
With little heating or cooling load expected in the U.S. this week, many were surprised by the cash rally and wondered where prices would go once broader air conditoning demand kicked in.
"A normal weather scenario should be bearish at this time of year, but prices continue to move up," a trader said.
Forecasts are calling for normal to below-normal weather for most of the nation into early June. Some above-normal temperatures are expected in parts of the Southeast and Southwest.

Chart traders said June's break today of resistance at $2.30 will likely to lead to a test of the $2.43 contract high before the spot month goes off the board Wednesday. Support was seen at $2.15 and then at the $2.05 double bottom.
Separately, Arizona Public Service said its Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit was expected back later today or tomorrow, while Texas Utilities said Comanche Peak 2 nuke should return to full power Tuesday.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed by about 10 cents Tuesday to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a dime or more to about $2.10. New York city gate gas was up about five cents to the high-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 38,192 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.

On KCBT, June jumped eight cents to $2.19, while deferreds were still steady to four cents higher. The June contract expires today. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 16.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
